title: Importing Lie Detection Psychology: Testing Whether Verbal Uncertainty Markers Predict Model Dishonesty
original_idea: Collect a dataset of model responses labeled as honest or sycophantic. Extract linguistic features (hedge words, certainty markers, modal verbs, sentence length changes). Train a simple classifier to predict dishonesty from these features.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If linguistic features predict dishonesty, cheap monitoring becomes possible. Practical safety tool potential.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Feature extraction and simple classification are standard CS skills. NLP feature engineering is accessible. Well-suited for CS students.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Data collection, labeling, feature extraction, classifier training, and evaluation. Could be done in 30hrs if dataset is small (100-200 examples).

novelty.reasoning: While linguistic features have been studied in LLM contexts (psycholinguistic marker extraction, linguistic features of AI misinformation), the specific application of human lie-detection psychology (hedge words, certainty markers, modal verbs, sentence length changes) as predictors of sycophantic dishonesty in LLMs is not directly addressed. Research on LLM uncertainty detection focuses on calibration and abstention rather than surface linguistic markers as dishonesty signals. The cross-disciplinary bridge from deception psychology to LLM monitoring is a distinctive angle.
